newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Niaga new owner sees insurance synergies.
newsitem.headline: Niaga new owner sees insurance synergies.

text.p: Indonesia's Tirtamas Group, which has announced the acquisition of the country's sixth-largest private bank, Bank Niaga, said on Tuesday that the deal will provide synergies with its other banking and insurance businesses.
Tirtamas chairman Hashim Djojohadikusumo told reporters that Bank Niaga's network of 62 branches was one of the attractions for the group.

"We are very much interested in the insurance business and we've always been looking for a distribution network," he said at a news conference. "So there are synergies not only in banking but also in insurance. The opportunity also presents itself for some consolidation of our banking business."

Tirtamas is best-known for its controlling interest in cement firm Semen Cibinong, but also has large stakes in several banks, including Bank Papan Sejahtera, Merrill Lynch Indonesia, Bank Kredit Asia and Bank Pelita.
It also has a joint venture with one of the world's largest insurance companies, Metropolitan Life Insurance Co of the United States, called MetLife Sejahtera Insurance.

Tirtamas announced on Monday that it will buy out the 40 percent stake held in Bank Niaga by controlling shareholders, the Tahija family, and also put out a tender offer for an additional 10 percent. The stake will be bought at 8,000 rupiah ($3.11) per share, it said.
Brokers and analysts have said the purchase will cost Tirtamas about 756 billion rupiah ($293.6 million).
Hashim said it was a fair price and added that the purchase would be funded by internal cash flows and the sale of some assets. He refused to give details.
An analyst at a foreign brokerage said the assets were likely to be in the group's cement division.
But Hashim said the group will not neglect the cement business, which provides the dominant share of group revenues.

"We're not shifting (focus) at all," he said. "Our present cement capacity is 7.1 million tonnes (per annum). By November we should be close to 10 million tonnes. We are very confident about the cement and building materials side of the business."
But banking analysts have said Hashim, who belongs to one of the most prominent families in Indonesia, is keen to make a mark in the banking sector.

He is the son of former cabinet minister Sumitro Djojohadikusumo, who is considered the czar of Indonesia's current economic policies; his brother, special forces commander Major-General Prabowo Subianto, is married to one of President Suharto's daughters while a sister is married to central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono.
Hashim said his father would be the president director of Bank Niaga. He added that Tirtamas intended to use the bank "as the platform for a regional presence".

"We also think it is good for Bank Niaga. With our network of contacts, with our good name in the international capital markets, we have the capability to strengthen the capital base of Bank Niaga. It's a win-win situation for all."
George Tahija, one of the sons of former Bank Niaga owner Julius Tahija, said his family decided to sell out to concentrate resources elsewhere.

"Banks are always hungry for capital and as a bank grows so does its need for capital," he told the news conference. "After a rights issue in 1996, we made a strategic decision not to inject further capital and look for opportunities to diversify. This was not an easy decision, but it was made easier after we received an offer from Tirtamas.
"Hashim understands the principles the bank abides by. It was a friendly transaction," he said, adding that the proceeds of the sale would be re-invested in other businesses within Indonesia.
